Account Closure Procedure

Procedure ID: MS-PRO-012 | Version 1.4 | Effective: June 1, 2026 | Owner: Member Services | Classification: Internal

1. Purpose

This procedure explains how Member Service Representatives (MSRs) and Member Contact Centre agents close Retail share and checking accounts at a member's request, and how remaining funds are returned. It does not cover closures initiated by Harbor for risk or policy reasons, which follow the Involuntary Closure Standard.

2. Before You Begin

Confirm that the request comes from an owner of the account. For joint accounts, every owner must consent to the closure. Review the account for linked services that will fail once the account is closed, including direct deposits, automatic loan payments, bill pay payees, and person-to-person

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 2. Before You Begin
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
linked services that will fail once the account is closed, including direct deposits, automatic loan payments, bill pay payees, and person-to-person payment enrollments, and explain to the member which services they need to redirect.

Closing the Primary Share Account ends the member's membership. If the member has an open loan, the Primary Share Account cannot be closed until the loan is paid in full.

3. Closure Steps

Step | Action | Owner
1 | Verify the member's identity using two forms of identification in branch or the three-factor authentication script by phone. | MSR or agent
2 | Obtain a signed Form HCU-ACL-220 (Account Closure Request) from every owner on the account. | MSR
3 | Review pending items, holds and scheduled transfers in the core system and note them on the form. | MSR

metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
from every owner on the account. | MSR
3 | Review pending items, holds and scheduled transfers in the core system and note them on the form. | MSR
4 | Cancel debit cards, stop recurring transfers and remove bill pay payees linked to the account. | MSR
5 | Move the account to Closing status and record the requested disbursement method. | MSR
6 | Complete the pending items review described in Section 4. | Deposit Operations
7 | Disburse the remaining balance as described in Section 5 and set the account to Closed. | Deposit Operations
8 | Send the closure confirmation letter and retain the form in the member file. | Deposit Operations

Phone requests may be accepted for single-owner accounts only, and the signed form must be returned by mail or secure upload before step 5 can be completed.

4. Pending Items Review

Accounts with outstanding checks, pending ACH debits or unresolved card disputes are placed in Closing status for a 30-day review period before final disbursement. During the review period, deposits are rejected and items presented for payment are paid only up to the remaining balance. Accounts with no pending items may be disbursed on the next business day.

5. Disbursement of Remaining Funds

After the review period, the remaining balance is disbursed by official check mailed within 7 business days to the address on file. At the member's request, funds may instead be transferred to another Harbor member's account with that

within 7 business days to the address on file. At the member's request, funds may instead be transferred to another Harbor member's account with that member's consent, or paid out in cash in branch if the balance is under $2,500. Dividends are paid through the date of closure.

If the account is overdrawn at closure, do not complete the closure. Refer the member to the Overdraft Policy and create a recovery case.

6. Worked Example

The check cleared on 06/22/2026, the

7. Records

Form HCU-ACL-220 and the closure confirmation letter are retained for five years after closure. Closed accounts are reported to the account screening agency only where the account was closed with a negative balance.

Business Checking Products

Business Essentials Checking has a monthly maintenance fee of $10.00, waived with an average daily balance of $2,500 or more. It includes 200 free transactions per statement cycle, after which each debit or deposited item is charged $0.40.

Card Dispute Procedure

Procedure ID: CS-PRO-031 | Revision 5 | Effective: April 15, 2026 | Owner: Card Services | Classification: Internal

1. Purpose

This procedure sets out how Member Contact Centre agents and Card Services analysts receive, classify, investigate and resolve disputes on Harbor debit and credit cards. It is designed to meet the error-resolution requirements of Regulation E for debit cards and Regulation Z for credit cards, and the chargeback rules of the card network.

2. Intake and Timeframes

Members must report an unauthorized or disputed card transaction within 60 days of the statement date on which the transaction first appeared. Disputes received after this period are still logged, but Harbor's liability protections and the member's right to provisional credit may

metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
appeared. Disputes received after this period are still logged, but Harbor's liability protections and the member's right to provisional credit may be limited.

For every dispute, the agent completes Form HCU-DSP-114 (Card Transaction Dispute) during the initial contact, whether the contact is by phone, in branch, or through secure message. The form captures the transaction date, amount, merchant descriptor, the member's explanation, and whether the card is still in the member's possession.

1. Verify the caller using the standard three-factor authentication script.

2. Confirm the transaction details against the card processing system.

3. If fraud is suspected, block the card immediately and order a replacement.

4. Complete Form HCU-DSP-114 and read the dispute acknowledgment

metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

4. Complete Form HCU-DSP-114 and read the dispute acknowledgment disclosure.

5. Route the case to the Card Services dispute queue in the case management system.

3. Classification

Card Services classifies each dispute within one business day of intake. Unauthorized transactions (lost, stolen or counterfeit card; card-not-present fraud) follow the fraud path. Authorized transactions with a merchant problem (goods not received, not as described, duplicate processing, credit not processed) follow the merchant dispute path. Where the member has not first tried to resolve a merchant dispute with the merchant, the analyst documents the reason in the case notes.

4. Provisional Credit

Provisional credit for the disputed amount is posted within 10 business days of receiving the dispute notice if the investigation has not been completed by then. For accounts opened less than 30 days before the first disputed transaction, provisional credit is posted within 20 business days. The member is notified of the provisional credit, including the amount and date, within two business days of posting.

Provisional credit is not required for credit card disputes, where the disputed amount is instead suspended from the balance and excluded from finance charges while the investigation is open.

5. Investigation

The investigation must be completed within 45 calendar days of receiving the dispute notice. The period is extended to 90 calendar days for point-of-sale transactions, foreign-initiated transactions, and transactions on accounts opened within the previous 30 days. The analyst reviews authorization data, device and location information, prior dispute history, and any documents supplied by the member or the merchant.

Where a chargeback is appropriate, Card Services submits it to the network no later than 120 calendar days after the transaction settlement date. Supporting documents are attached to the case record, not stored on shared drives.

Complaints about the handling of a dispute are logged in the complaint register in accordance with the Complaint Handling Standard.

Debit Card Limits and Controls

Member guide | Updated: February 2, 2026 | Applies to: Harbor Visa® debit cards on Retail checking accounts

Your Harbor debit card has daily limits that protect your account if the card is lost, stolen or used without your permission. This guide explains the limits, how to change them, and the controls you can set yourself in the Harbor mobile app — no phone call needed.

Daily Limits

For most members, the standard daily ATM cash withdrawal limit is $500. The card’s daily point-of-sale purchase limit is $3,000, which covers purchases made in stores, online and by phone. Limits reset at midnight Eastern Time. Cash back received at a store counts toward the purchase limit, not the ATM limit.

Premier Checking cardholders may have higher limits based on their

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Daily Limits
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Cash back received at a store counts toward the purchase limit, not the ATM limit.

Premier Checking cardholders may have higher limits based on their relationship with Harbor. Your current limits are shown in the app under Card Controls — Limits.

Requesting a Temporary Increase

If you need to make a large purchase — for example, a car deposit or a café renovation invoice — you can request a temporary increase through the Member Contact Centre or at a branch. Temporary increases last up to 72 hours. We’ll ask you to verify your identity and may ask about the purpose of the transaction. Increases are approved at Harbor’s discretion and are not available on accounts open less than 60 days.

Card Controls in the App

- Lock and unlock your card – a locked card declines new purchases and ATM

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Requesting a Temporary Increase
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
available on accounts open less than 60 days.

Card Controls in the App

- Lock and unlock your card – a locked card declines new purchases and ATM withdrawals, while recurring payments you’ve already set up continue.

- Turn international transactions on or off – transactions outside the United States are declined while this control is off.

- Set spending alerts – receive a notification for any purchase above an amount you choose.

- Block merchant categories – for example, gaming or online marketplaces.

Changes to card controls take effect immediately. Locking your card is not the same as reporting it lost or stolen; if you can’t find your card after checking, report it right away so we can block it and order a replacement.

Travelling

You don’t need to tell us before you travel, but

Travelling

You don’t need to tell us before you travel, but keeping your phone number and e-mail address up to date helps us reach you if we see unusual activity. Foreign transaction fees are listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges.

Your Liability

Tell us at once if you believe your card has been lost or stolen. Your liability for unauthorized transactions is explained in the Electronic Fund Transfer Agreement and Disclosure you received when you opened your account — a plain-language résumé of the key points is available on request.

_Policy number: LN-COL-002 | Version 1.6 | Effective date: May 1, 2026 | Owner: Consumer Lending and Collections_

1. Purpose

This policy describes how Harbor Credit Union treats consumer loan payments that are not received by the due date, the fees that apply, the communications members receive, and the point at which an account is referred for collection. It is intended to balance fair treatment of members experiencing difficulty with the credit union's duty to protect the membership as a whole from loan losses.

2. Scope

This policy applies to closed-end consumer loans, including new and used auto loans, personal loans, and share-secured loans. Credit card accounts, home equity lines of credit and first mortgages are covered by their own

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 2. Scope

text:
auto loans, personal loans, and share-secured loans. Credit card accounts, home equity lines of credit and first mortgages are covered by their own agreements and servicing procedures.

3. Grace Period

A payment is considered late if it is not received within 15 calendar days after the due date shown on the billing statement. Payments received during the grace period are applied as on-time payments for fee purposes, although interest continues to accrue daily on simple-interest loans until the payment is received.

If the last day of the grace period falls on a weekend or a Federal Reserve holiday, the grace period is extended to the next business day.

4. Late Fees

When a payment is late under Section 3, Harbor assesses a single late fee equal to 5% of the scheduled payment amount or

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 3. Grace Period
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
business day.

4. Late Fees

When a payment is late under Section 3, Harbor assesses a single late fee equal to 5% of the scheduled payment amount or $25.00, whichever is less. Only one late fee is charged for any one scheduled payment, and a late fee is never charged because an earlier late fee remains unpaid. Late fees are not charged on loans enrolled in an approved hardship program while the member is meeting the program terms.

5. Delinquency Communications

1. Day 5 after the due date: courtesy reminder by e-mail or text alert.

2. Day 16: late notice by mail stating the late fee and the amount now due.

3. Day 30: outbound call from a Collections Specialist to discuss the reason for the delay and repayment options.

4. Day 45: second written notice offering a hardship review

metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
from a Collections Specialist to discuss the reason for the delay and repayment options.

4. Day 45: second written notice offering a hardship review appointment.

5. Day 60: notice of right to cure, where required by state law.

6. Credit Reporting

Harbor reports an account as delinquent to the consumer reporting agencies once a payment is 30 or more days past due. Reporting is accurate and complete, and disputes of credit reporting are investigated within the timeframes required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

7. Collections Referral

Accounts that reach 90 days past due are transferred from the Collections Specialist team to the Recovery Unit. The Recovery Unit may recommend repossession of collateral, legal action, or placement with an outside agency, subject to approval by the

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 7. Collections Referral
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Unit. The Recovery Unit may recommend repossession of collateral, legal action, or placement with an outside agency, subject to approval by the Collections Manager. All collection activity must comply with applicable consumer protection laws, and members may not be contacted before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. local time.

8. Hardship Assistance

Members experiencing temporary hardship may request a payment extension, a skip-a-payment, or a loan modification. A loan may receive no more than two payment extensions in any rolling 12-month period. Hardship requests are reviewed within five business days of receiving the member's completed application and supporting documents.

9. Charge-Off

Consumer loans that remain delinquent are charged off no later than 120 days past due for closed-end

and supporting documents.

Consumer loans that remain delinquent are charged off no later than 120 days past due for closed-end loans, unless the Collections Manager documents a reasonable expectation of recovery. Charge-off does not release the member from the obligation to repay.

1. Purpose

This standard documents the rule thresholds used by the real-time fraud monitoring platform for Retail accounts. Disclosure of these thresholds would allow fraudsters to structure activity to avoid detection. Access is limited to Enterprise Fraud Risk, the Fraud Response Team, Internal Audit and designated Information Security staff.

2. Card Velocity Rules

Velocity Rule VR-5 triggers when a card is used at ATMs in two different states within 90 minutes. Velocity Rule VR-7 triggers when three (3) or more declined PIN attempts occur within 24 hours at different terminals.

3. Account Takeover Indicators

An account takeover score of 720 or above places an online banking session in step-up authentication. A change of phone number or e-mail address followed within 72 hours by an external transfer of more than $2,000 generates a priority alert for manual review.

Person-to-person payments above $800 to a first-time recipient are delayed by four hours. Wire requests are governed by the Wire Transfer Policy; the monitoring platform additionally scores every outgoing wire above $15,000 for account takeover risk.

Thresholds are reviewed monthly by the Fraud Rules Committee using false-positive rates, confirmed fraud losses and member friction metrics. Changes are documented in the rules change log and approved by the Chief Risk Officer. Emergency changes may be made by the Fraud Response Team lead and must be ratified at the next committee meeting.

Policy number: PAY-WT-004 | Revision 2026-02 | Effective date: February 16, 2026 | Owner: Payments Operations | Applies to: Retail accounts

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements Harbor Credit Union follows when sending and receiving funds transfers by wire on behalf of Retail members. Wire transfers are generally final once sent and are a frequent target of fraud, so the controls in this policy are designed to confirm that every outgoing wire is authorized by the member, is accurate, and complies with applicable law, including Article 4A of the Uniform Commercial Code, the Bank Secrecy Act, and sanctions screening requirements.

2. Scope

This policy applies to domestic and international wire transfers initiated from or received into Retail share and

metadata.section_path: 1. Purpose

text:

2. Scope

This policy applies to domestic and international wire transfers initiated from or received into Retail share and checking accounts. Business accounts are subject to the Business Account Fee Guide and the Business Services Agreement. Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfers, person-to-person payments, and internal transfers between Harbor accounts are not wire transfers and are outside the scope of this policy.

3. Definitions

Business day means Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Reserve holidays.

Domestic wire means a funds transfer to a beneficiary account at a financial institution located in the United States.

International wire means a funds transfer to a beneficiary account at a financial institution located outside the United States, in US

metadata.section_path: 3. Definitions

text:
United States.

International wire means a funds transfer to a beneficiary account at a financial institution located outside the United States, in US dollars or a foreign currency.

Callback verification means a telephone call placed by Harbor staff to a phone number already on file for the member, not a number supplied in the wire request.

4. Authorized Channels

Members may request an outgoing wire in person at any Harbor branch or through online banking once the member has enrolled in online wire service. The Member Contact Centre may answer questions about a wire but does not accept wire instructions by telephone, e-mail or text message. Instructions received by e-mail must be treated as a potential fraud attempt and reported to the Fraud Response Team.

Online wire service is available to members whose account has been open for at least 90 days and who have completed enhanced authentication enrollment. The online daily limit for outgoing wires is $50,000 per member. Requests above this limit must be completed in branch with valid government-issued photo identification.

5. Processing Cutoff Times

Domestic wire requests received and verified by 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day are processed the same business day. Requests received after the cutoff, or on a day that is not a business day, are processed on the next business day. International wire requests must be received and verified by 1:00 p.m. Eastern

International wire requests must be received and verified by 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time to be released the same business day; delivery to the beneficiary may take one to five business days depending on the destination country and intermediary banks.

6. Fees

The fee for an outgoing domestic wire from a Retail account is $25.00 per wire. Outgoing international wires from Retail accounts are charged $45.00 per wire, plus any intermediary or beneficiary bank charges deducted from the transferred amount. Incoming wires credited to a Retail account are charged $15.00 per wire. Fees are debited from the funding account at the time the wire is sent or received and are not refunded if a wire is returned by the receiving

7. Verification and Fraud Controls

Any online wire request above $25,000 requires a callback verification before release. Branch wire requests require the member to sign the wire request form in the presence of staff after the details have been read back. Every outgoing wire is screened against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions lists before release; a potential match places the wire on hold until Compliance clears or rejects it.

Staff must place a wire on hold and escalate to the Fraud Response Team if the member appears to be acting under instruction from a third party, if the request follows a recent

8. Errors, Recalls and Returns

A member who believes a wire was sent in error must notify Harbor as soon as possible. Harbor will request a recall from the receiving institution but cannot guarantee the return of funds once a wire has been released. Returned funds are credited to the member's account net of any charges imposed by the receiving or intermediary institutions.

Exceptions to this policy, including fee waivers above $100 in a calendar year for a single member, require written approval from the Payments Operations Manager. Exceptions to the verification requirements in Section 7 are not permitted.

How do I become a member of Harbor Credit Union?

Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in our service area, and their immediate family members, can join. A minimum deposit of $5.00 in a Primary Share Account establishes your membership. You can open your membership online in about ten minutes or at any branch.

What are the Member Contact Centre hours?

Paying People and Bills

How much can I send with Harbor Pay?

Harbor Pay person-to-person payments are limited to $1,000 per day and $3,000 per rolling 30 days. Payments to a recipient you have paid before usually arrive within minutes.

When will my bill payment arrive?

Electronic bill payments are delivered within two business days. Payees that cannot accept electronic payments receive a paper check, which can take up to five business days.
